Theorem
[Borsuk--Ulam theorem, dimension 2]

↗ thm:fundamental-group-of-circle

1. ch1:1.10\group Fundamental Group

For every continuous $f:S^2\to \R ^2$, there is $x\in S^2$ with $f(x)=f(-x)$.

Proof

\sketch Otherwise $g(x)=(f(x)-f(-x))/|f(x)-f(-x)|$ maps $S^2$ to $S^1$ and satisfies $g(-x)=-g(x)$. A lift on the equator changes by $q/2$ after half a turn for an odd integer $q$, so the equatorial loop has nonzero degree. It is also the image under $g$ of a loop contracting in $S^2$, a contradiction.

□
